{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABiyEOlw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhMItJs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 150, "title": "Implement persistent full-machine save states with a unified screenshot-based picker", "body": "## Problem

The browser player remembers ROMs and cartridge-native progress but cannot capture and restore an arbitrary point in gameplay. Add full-machine save states and a simple management UI, following the latest sibling snes-rust design rather than its earlier separate Save/Load dialogs.

## Expected outcome

- A versioned, compressed, ROM-free snapshot of the emulated machine can be captured and restored while playing or paused, without rebooting.
- Persistent browser-local IndexedDB history, scoped by full raw ROM SHA-256 and physical console model, with actual framebuffer thumbnails and timestamps.
- One shared **Save state** selector, with **New state**, existing entries, Delete and Import/Export, plus separate explicit **Save** and **Load** actions. Selection alone never saves or loads. First save creates and selects a state; subsequent saves overwrite that selected state atomically. Load is disabled for New state.
- Preserve ordinary cartridge SRAM/EEPROM, RTC and model-specific internal EEPROM records, including recoverable backups before a state restore would replace newer persistent data. No multiple native-save profiles in this milestone.
- Keep management controls above gameplay on touch devices and outside gameplay-only fullscreen. Preserve the existing controller, orientation, audio, ROM library and automatic visibility resume.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline main: [19ec2e4](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/19ec2e41857800a6f498cac5d88d38d3b833adc0). Inspect current main before implementation.

References: sibling [snes-rust #180](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/180), [#182](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/182), [#184](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/184), [#186](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/186), [snapshot format documentation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/save-states.md). Use the final unified picker design and lessons about proportionate scope, not SNES-specific state fields, normalized ROM hashes, SRAM profiles or elaborate cross-tab recovery machinery.

Inspect crates/ws-core (Machine, CPU, bus, video, audio, cartridge, mapper, EEPROM, RTC, IPL and timing), crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs, web/src/main.ts, web/src/saves.ts, current cartridge-library helpers, web/index.html and web/src/style.css. Existing raw ROM identity is wonderswan:save:v1:<sha256>; preserve existing storage keys and records. Related #138, #140, #142, #146, #148.

### Snapshot core and format

- Define a documented versioned binary envelope with ROM hash, physical model, format version and bounded compressed/uncompressed lengths. Use a maintained Rust serialization/compression approach compatible with native and Wasm. Do not serialize ROM bytes, built-in IPL binaries, host handles, browser preferences or host audio queues. Reuse immutable ROM/firmware from the currently loaded machine.
- Capture at a consistent execution boundary. Include all mutable state needed for deterministic continuation: CPU registers/flags/prefetch and interrupt state, RAM, bus/mapper and IPL lockout, video including raster latches and framebuffer, sound channels and timing, DMA/timers, keypad/interrupt latches, cartridge SRAM/EEPROM including in-flight operations, internal EEPROM/protection, RTC and scheduler/device counters. Audit actual structs and document derived caches that are reconstructed rather than serialized. Preserve physical-model and cartridge configuration invariants.
- Validate envelope, version, identity, model, lengths, enums, indices and device invariants before replacing live state. Bound file size and decompression/allocation; reject truncated, corrupt, incompatible or wrong-ROM/model states without partial mutation or panic. No promise of cross-version compatibility beyond documented supported format; reject unsupported versions clearly. No third-party state format support.
- Restore through native and Wasm APIs without executing a reset or IPL again. Flush stale host input/audio, redraw captured frame, reset host pacing timestamps and presentation history, preserve user playback intent and visibility/Help constraints. Document RTC policy: restore captured guest clock/device state consistently, rebase host wall-clock anchor so elapsed time since snapshot capture does not accidentally advance the restored state; retain ordinary RTC behavior thereafter. Test deterministic replay with controlled clock/input.

### Persistent data safety

- Existing normal save keys and data remain readable without migration. Before applying a snapshot that would change cartridge SRAM/EEPROM, RTC or physical-model internal EEPROM, validate the entire candidate and persist an accessible recovery copy of the outgoing current records (including current live nonvolatile bytes). If required backup cannot be committed or existing records are unreadable, refuse the destructive restore and leave live machine and prior records intact. Do not silently bypass existing blocked-save safeguards.
- Provide a simple documented way to export/recover those backup records (e.g. recovery snapshot with clear label and the same picker/export workflow, containing outgoing machine and nonvolatile state, with protection for any differing persisted records). Ensure the user can actually recover the previous progress; do not merely write inaccessible backup keys. Use the smallest coherent single-tab transaction/rollback strategy; account for IndexedDB versus localStorage not sharing a transaction. Do not claim atomicity across stores. Prevent routine autosave from overwriting preserved records after a failed restore. Verify ordinary failure paths and successful recovery. No exhaustive compound-failure durability guarantee.
- Removing a remembered ROM or deleting a state must not erase normal save records or other states. Reset continues to preserve completed saves. Scope state selection by ROM and model; no implicit model switch on Load.

### Browser UI and storage

- Use a separate versioned WonderSwan-specific IndexedDB namespace. Store compressed binary, stable ID, timestamp and actual screenshot together atomically; enumerate lightweight metadata/thumbnails without decoding all snapshots. Use a bounded page or lazy list for large histories. No arbitrary fixed slot cap; storage capacity is the limit. No uploads.
- Compact toolbar group: [Save state: New state / selected entry ▾] [Save] [Load]. One accessible scrollable picker with thumbnails, dates, selection indicator, New state, per-entry Delete (confirm target) and Export, and Import. Keep state management distinct from native saves. Selecting/dismissing does not mutate gameplay or storage. Save creates/selects after commit or overwrites selected ID without growing count; failed overwrite retains previous snapshot and thumbnail. Delete selected returns to New state. Import validates and creates a distinct entry, never implicitly loads or overwrites. Export excludes ROM bytes. Keep selection per ROM/model during session; reload selection persistence optional.
- Capture actual framebuffer thumbnail at same boundary as snapshot, respecting effective presentation orientation without baking host shader/UI into machine state. Save while playing or paused, with brief success feedback only after persistence. Load restores the chosen snapshot and preserves playing/paused intent. Prevent overlapping operations from targeting another cartridge/model; disable inappropriate actions while pending. Errors are clear and recoverable; ordinary play remains available when storage fails.
- Preserve modal focus, cancellation/backdrop dismissal without click-through, keyboard and touch usability, all eleven 44px game targets, safe areas and existing gameplay-only fullscreen. Management UI stays outside fullscreen and away from gameplay buttons. Use existing UI patterns, no new framework or management page.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Native tests and real production Wasm tests capture/restore representative original CC0 fixtures and demonstrate deterministic continuation with identical controlled input/clock, including CPU, video, audio, DMA/timing and nonvolatile state. Cover all three physical models with focused cases, including a boot/lockout boundary where supported. Verify wrong ROM/model/version, corrupt/truncated/oversized and invalid state rejection without live mutation; bounded decoding and no ROM content in exported format.
- [ ] Browser tests demonstrate New state, create, overwrite, select without side effects, explicit Load, delete, import/export, reload persistence, actual matching thumbnail, ROM/model isolation and lightweight history browsing. Verify running/paused restore and existing visibility, audio and input lifecycle.
- [ ] With original save/RTC/console fixtures, demonstrate older-state restore preserves recoverable outgoing progress, recovery works, existing saves survive upgrade and ROM removal, and representative failed backup/overwrite/invalid restore leaves prior data and live state safe. Test ordinary single-tab storage failures, not exhaustive combinations.
- [ ] Verify keyboard/touch picker, cancellation/focus, no accidental save/load from backdrop or gameplay, and reachable game/management controls in representative 375×812, 812×375 and 320×568 viewports, both game orientations as applicable. Scrolling is acceptable in constrained layouts. Preserve existing fullscreen, orientation, display effects and controller behavior; no pixel-by-pixel viewport optimization.
- [ ] Document snapshot format/version policy, recovery workflow, local-only storage and limitations in README/Help and a concise technical document. Run python3 fixtures/build.py --check, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --workspace --locked, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, git diff --check, and web npm ci, npm run build:wasm, npm run build, npm run test:browser and npm run test:compat against production preview. Reuse existing fixtures/builds and relevant coverage. Record actual results and limitations.

### Completion and scope discipline

Normal single-tab usage is the supported workflow. Concurrent editing of the same ROM/model across tabs may be documented unsupported or rejected with a simple guard. No cross-tab reconciliation, journals, automatic eviction, cloud sync, native-save profiles, rewind, autosnapshots, or exhaustive quota/navigation/process-crash combinations. No guarantee of durability under browser eviction or abrupt termination. Concrete data loss in ordinary use, incorrect restoration, unsafe decoding, inaccessible essential controls and required test failures remain blocking. Minor visual polish, hypothetical compound failures and extreme viewport optimization do not block merge. Do not expand the acceptance matrix during review or repeatedly rerun unchanged checks without reason. Once the requested behavior and mandatory gates pass with no material supported-use defect, approve, merge and close. No human approval, physical phone, commercial ROM or proprietary BIOS is required.

## Optional validation

Mobile WebKit, physical phone, larger histories and measured snapshot latency/size if useful. No exhaustive stress matrix or arbitrary performance target.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge and closure, verify Pages deployment of the merge revision and smoke-test the published player with original CC0 fixtures: create, overwrite, reload, select/load, export/import and recover outgoing progress. Record actual results, workflow URL and limitations. Pending publication checks are not pre-merge blockers; confirmed production defects get linked follow-up issues.
